description: Add Runner-local Provider rate-limit backpressure, bounded throttling retries, and first-class Workflow rate-limit outcomes.

tasks.title: Enforce shared Provider admission in the Runner
tasks.description: Add the validated Provider concurrency policy, canonical Provider-key resolution, and a RunnerHost-owned ProviderAdmissionController with independent FIFO queues, permit accounting, and cancellation-aware waiters. Inject and enforce the shared controller at the actual request boundary used by Pi, OpenCode, Workflow Agent executions, and AgentJobs while preserving the existing Runner-slot and Agent concurrency gates.
acceptanceCriteria: Runner configuration accepts a validated default Provider limit, per-Provider overrides, and rate-limit wait/backoff settings, and invalid values produce the existing actionable startup diagnostic without admitting work.

Two concurrent requests from different Agents or Workflow runs that resolve to the same canonical Provider share one FIFO admission queue and never exceed that Provider's configured in-flight request limit; different Provider keys proceed independently.
Admission is acquired immediately before each actual model request and released on success, failure, or cancellation; no lease is held while a request is waiting for retry backoff.
Cancellation removes a queued waiter promptly, sends no model request, and leaves the Provider permit count correct for later work.
Existing Runner capacity and Agent-level concurrency limits remain enforced and compose with Provider admission without bypass or capacity increase.

Deterministic Runner tests with queued fake requests and injected cancellation/fake time cover same-Provider sharing, different-Provider independence, FIFO release, queued cancellation, and composition with the existing Runner and Agent gates.
tasks.output: A configured, Runner-local ProviderAdmissionController integrated into the shared Pi/OpenCode request path and covered by deterministic admission tests.
tasks.notes: Use the runtime's canonical Provider ID as the key; do not place unresolved Providers into a shared unknown bucket. The limiter is intentionally process-local to one Runner execution plane.

tasks.title: Implement bounded Provider rate-limit retry
tasks.description: Replace threshold-only 429 handling at the shared runtime request boundary with a normalized ProviderRateLimitSignal and an independent bounded retry coordinator. Update the Pi and OpenCode adapters to expose one Provider attempt at a time, honor valid Retry-After values or configured fallback backoff, emit waiting facts, preserve cancellation semantics, and return structured provider-rate-limited results on deadline expiry.
acceptanceCriteria: Pi and OpenCode recognize HTTP 429 and documented equivalent structured or configured-pattern signals, retain the canonical Provider and throttling facts, and do not classify the first recognized signal as turn-failed.

Each rate-limit retry reacquires Provider admission and releases it after that attempt; the permit is not held during Retry-After or fallback backoff, and opaque SDK replay cannot bypass this attempt boundary.

A valid Retry-After seconds value or HTTP date is honored for at least the declared delay when within the remaining bound; absent or unusable values use the configured fallback policy, and no request is sent after the absolute deadline.

Rate-limit delays and attempts use a budget independent of the ordinary consecutive Provider retry budget, so a sequence that recovers after the ordinary threshold reports normal success while genuine non-rate-limit failures retain their existing classification.

Persistent throttling returns status and error code provider-rate-limited with Provider identity, latest signal, first-throttled time, deadline, last and next attempt times, attempt count, and accumulated wait facts.

Cancellation during admission or backoff interrupts promptly, prevents the next request, releases any held permit, and preserves the existing cancellation or interruption classification rather than becoming provider-rate-limited.

Deterministic Pi/OpenCode tests with fake Providers, fake clocks, queued requests, Retry-After variants, fallback backoff, ordinary retry failures, recovery, deadline expiry, SDK attempt boundaries, and cancellation verify all criteria.
tasks.output: Pi and OpenCode produce bounded, structured Provider rate-limit retry results and waiting events through the shared runtime request boundary.
tasks.notes: Keep normal transport, deadline, cleanup, and generation-quarantine behavior unchanged. Rate-limit waiting must not consume the ordinary Provider retry counter.

tasks.title: Publish durable Workflow rate-limit waiting state
tasks.description: Carry typed Provider admission and backoff waiting events through the existing runtime observer, transcript allowlist, Runner outbox, AgentSession binding validation, and Session-to-Workflow observation path. Record the latest waiting facts on the active TaskRun and expose a nonterminal provider-rate-limit-waiting projection without advancing the stage, settling the task, or creating duplicate work.
acceptanceCriteria: The runtime event payload distinguishes admission from backoff and carries Provider key, latest status/message, Retry-After when present, next-attempt time, wait deadline when applicable, remaining wait, and attempt count.

WorkflowAgentSessionReporter, the runtime-event outbox, transcript allowlisting, AgentSessionGrain binding validation, and ISessionWorkPort preserve and deliver the typed waiting observation without encoding rate-limit facts in an error string.

A waiting observation updates the current Agent execution's ProviderRateLimitState while the task remains unfinished and its result settlement remains AwaitingResult; repeated observations update latest facts without extending the absolute throttle deadline.
Admission waiting remains cancellable and visible without a throttle expiry deadline until a Provider signal exists, and waiting does not dispatch a second attempt or duplicate work.

Server status mapping exposes provider-rate-limit-waiting with the Provider and known timing facts, leaves task/stage/run nonterminal, does not advance the stage, and preserves existing success and genuine failure projections.

Deterministic Session and Workflow tests verify event persistence/replay and binding validation, admission versus backoff observations, deadline stability, cancellation visibility, nonterminal status, no stage advancement, and no duplicate dispatch.
tasks.output: A durable, replayable Workflow waiting projection for Provider admission and rate-limit backoff.
tasks.notes: Waiting is a projection aid; the Runner work-result journal remains authoritative for terminal expiry. Use the existing ordered outbox and binding-validated Session event path.

tasks.title: Add terminal Provider rate-limit Workflow recovery
tasks.description: Extend Runner result/report contracts, translation, Workflow lifecycle transitions, persistence, status mapping, and retry control so bounded throttling expiry remains a first-class provider-rate-limited outcome. Persist structured ProviderRateLimitState, keep it distinct from FailureDetails and TaskFailed, expose the recoverable retry target, and ensure retry re-enters normal Runner, Agent, and Provider admission.
acceptanceCriteria: A bounded Runner expiry is translated by WorkflowItemTranslator and the authoritative report path as provider-rate-limited with all structured Provider timing facts preserved; it is never reduced only to TaskReportStatus.Failed, FailureReason.TaskFailed, or turn-failed.

Workflow task, stage, and run transitions represent provider-rate-limited as a recoverable explicit outcome, do not mark the run permanently terminal, do not emit Action/artifact/follow-up/TaskFailed outputs, and clear or retain ProviderRateLimitState according to successful recovery, ordinary failure, or expiry semantics.

ProviderRateLimitState is additive and serializer-compatible: existing persisted success, genuine failure, cancellation, and in-flight records deserialize with unchanged meaning, while expired rate-limit facts survive persistence and reload without a database migration.

The expired status projection exposes provider-rate-limited with Provider, latest signal, wait bound, and retry timing facts, while ordinary runtime, invalid-input, cancellation, quota, billing, and task failures retain their existing categories and details.

An expired task or run exposes the existing run-scoped retry operation with a rate-limit-specific target; retry clears the expired state, creates the normal new attempt, and passes through Runner, Agent, and Provider admission without automatic resubmission during waiting or expiry.

Server contract, transition, persistence reload, report journal/retry, retry re-admission, and regression tests verify exact category/fact preservation, absence of generic failure events, recovery behavior, and unchanged genuine failure handling.
tasks.output: Server and Workflow support for durable provider-rate-limited expiry, explicit recovery, and migration-free contract compatibility.
tasks.notes: Use append-only serializer IDs for new domain fields. The new status/category is a coordinated release contract for all consumers.

tasks.title: Expose rate-limit states in CLI and Web
tasks.description: Update CLI JSON/table models and Web workflow unions, status views, task rows, status pills, and available-action derivation for provider-rate-limit-waiting and provider-rate-limited. Render structured Provider and timing facts, keep waiting nonterminal and non-retryable, and expose the explicit recovery action only after expiry without falling back to a generic failure presentation.
acceptanceCriteria: CLI structured output and table views handle provider-rate-limit-waiting and show the affected Provider plus known next-attempt or remaining-wait information while treating the workflow as nonterminal.

Web status models and rendering handle both new wire categories without exhaustive-union fallbacks, display Provider and throttling timing facts, and distinguish waiting from expiry and genuine failure.
Waiting exposes no immediate retry action and is not rendered as completed or failed; expiry exposes the available rate-limit recovery action and its target without automatic resubmission.
CLI and Web retain the existing presentation and action behavior for success, genuine runtime/task failure, invalid input, cancellation, and other non-rate-limit outcomes.
CLI JSON/table and Web contract/component tests verify exact wire category and field preservation, waiting/expiry action rules, readable timing/provider rendering, and no generic TaskFailed fallback.
tasks.output: CLI and Web consumers render actionable Provider rate-limit waiting and expiry states with compatible existing behavior.
tasks.notes: Update Server, CLI, and Web in the same compatible release because the new status/category values are coordinated breaking contract changes.
